user_request: How can a supervisor coordinate specialized agents using shared state?

research_results.title: Shared state and communication
research_results.content: A shared state object carries the user request, intermediate research, retrieved documents, analysis, validation, errors, and final response between agents. Agents communicate by returning structured results to the supervisor.

research_results.title: Supervisor and specialized agents
research_results.content: A supervisor decomposes a request, delegates bounded tasks to specialized agents, receives their results, and chooses the next action. Keeping the supervisor in the loop makes ownership and control flow explicit.

research_results.title: Coordination costs and failure modes
research_results.content: Multiple agents can add latency, duplicated work, conflicting conclusions, and more failure points. Clear task ownership, bounded delegation, validation, and observable handoffs help manage those costs.

research_results.title: When a single agent becomes difficult to scale
research_results.content: A single agent that plans, retrieves, reasons, validates, and writes can accumulate a large prompt and tangled responsibilities. Complex tasks are harder to debug, parallelize, and verify when intermediate ownership is implicit.

retrieved_documents.title: Shared state and agent communication
retrieved_documents.content: Shared state is the typed handoff between agents. Agents return results rather than silently changing workflow ownership. The supervisor records each result before selecting the next step.

retrieved_documents.title: Multi-agent workflow limitations
retrieved_documents.content: Multi-agent systems add coordination overhead, latency, and more opportunities for failure. Shared state, bounded tasks, clear ownership, and validation improve observability but do not guarantee factual correctness.

retrieved_documents.title: Agent specialization and task ownership
retrieved_documents.content: Specialization gives each agent a bounded responsibility and a clear result contract. The supervisor owns delegation and workflow progress; a research agent finds candidate sources; a RAG agent retrieves relevant local passages.
